title: Multi-Tier Dependency Attenuation: region-aware pool and fallback orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a multi-tier attenuation layer that reduces end-to-end user-visible error and tail latency during degraded downstream conditions. This ticket delivers a region-aware connection pooling and fallback orchestration component that: (1) applies soft admission controls and progressive load-shedding per-tenant, (2) orchestrates fast local fallback to warm read-replicas or cache-promoted results, and (3) transparently hedges critical short RPCs across regionally proximate replicas when local latency spikes. The solution must preserve SLOs for p50/p95/p99 latency and error budget burn targets, minimize cross-region blast radius, and be configurable per-customer and per-route.
acceptance_criteria: Region-aware pool routes requests to the healthiest local pool by default and only fans out to secondary regions per-policy.
Admission controller exposes per-tenant QPS budget and rejects with 429 when exceeded; configurable soft-threshold and emergency-threshold.
Fallback policy supports two modes: cached-read promotion (for short-lived KV responses) and stale-read with TTL decay (for DB reads).
Circuit-breaker state transitions observable in Console with per-route metrics and traces (open/half-open/closed).
End-to-end integration tests simulate Redis/Kafka/DB slowdowns and show <=30% reduction in p99 error rate vs baseline without attenuation for affected routes.
Playbook and runbook added to Confluence describing mitigation steps and rollback knobs.
implementation_notes: Design a lightweight admission controller placed in the service edge prior to RPC fan-out; it should consult cached per-tenant budgets and approximate active connection counts.
Connection pool will expose ‘soft slots’ and ‘hard slots’ — soft slots allow latency-sensitive hedging while hard slots gate absolute concurrency to downstream nodes.
Fallback selection ranking: (1) local cache/prefix-KV, (2) read-replica in-region, (3) read-replica in-secondary-region (only if hedging policy allows).
Circuit breaker uses rolling-window failure rate + latency amplification signal; integrate with existing SLO alerting and tracing spans.
For Kafka consumer dependencies, implement backpressure by shrinking fetch size and deferring non-critical consumers, exposing consumer-priority lanes.
Implement feature flags to stage rollout per-account and per-region; defaulting off for high-risk tenants.
Benchmark plans: synthetic slowdowns (sleep 100ms/300ms/1s) and connection-surge tests; record cost delta for hedging scenarios.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and Product — agreed to preserve per-tenant SLO isolation. Action: SRE to provide historical p95/p99 latency slices for Redis and DB over last 90 days (Assigned to Priya).
2026-03-04: Prototype of admission controller created (internal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287). Initial API is feature-flagged and uses in-memory budgets.

2026-03-06: Design review feedback from Runtime and Console teams — require additional observability hooks (token-level correlation) and a Console UI for visualizing attenuation state. Added to scope.

2026-03-08: Integration test harness for injecting latency into Redis and DB implemented (kitchen sink load generator). Early results show 18% improvement in p99 errors for cached-read fallback scenarios.
2026-03-10: Security review triage — no KMS/HSM changes required. Decided to add audit logging for fallback activations per tenant (Console event stream).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive hedging reduces tail latency but increases cross-region egress and cost; we will default hedging to read-heavy, low-cardinality routes.
We will initially target Redis and read-only DB paths; write-heavy DB paths will use a conservative fallback (stale-read only after explicit consent).
Rollout plan: internal canary -> 5 pilot customers (opt-in) -> general availability behind Console toggle.
